channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nvidia Preparing to Oust CEO Jensen Huang: WSJ
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal said Wednesday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Germany Delays New Taxes, Power-Tax Cut, Rolls Back Welfare Cuts
item.description: The parties in Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s ruling coalition rolled back some planned social-spending cuts and delayed new taxes, clearing the way for a deal on Germany’s 2027 budget.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: Big Take: Huang's Scandal Will Push Democrats on US-China Policy
item.description: Today’s Big Take podcast digs into the geopolitical legacy President Trump is trying to cement in his final two years in office, even as a new majority Democratic Congress aims to rein him in on trade and foreign intervention. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: CoreWeave Triggers Rally
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A gauge for emerging-market stocks rose for a third day, led by Asian chipmakers, as strong CoreWeave sales and signs of demand for Anthropic’s planned IPO fueled optimism over AI spending. CoreWeave shares gain as much as 18%, in biggest jump since August, after the cloud-computing provider boosts its annual revenue forecast. Analysts said the results ease worries about the company’s financing, although concerns remain.
On today’s episode:
Brody Ford, Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Bailey Lipschultz, Bloomberg News Senior IPO Reporter Jenny Rooke, Genoa Ventures Founder & Managing Director (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: House Democrats Respond to White House Threat Over Coming Probes
item.description: House Democrats said Wednesday they wouldn't be intimidated or deterred by threats from President Trump's top lawyer over expected investigations in the next Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race, CNN Projects
item.description: Democrats padded their US Senate majority with a surprise win by Scott Colom, a district attorney who ousted Mississippi Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a reliably Republican state that President Donald Trump won by more than 22 percentage points in 2024, CNN projected.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Schumer Faces Progressive Push for Bolder Agenda After Midterm Rout
item.description: Some Democrats don’t give their Senate leader credit for their party’s electoral success.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Democrats Have a Tool to Fix the Labor Market
item.description: Fixing the job market should be the Democrats' top priority, says economist and Bloomberg Opinion columnist Kathryn Anne Edwards. Survey data can add context and give visibility to the issues workers have long complained is missing in unemployment data. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Earnings Triggers AI Boost
item.description: CoreWeave shares jumped after the company eased fears about its debt-laden business and signaled strong sales growth despite headwinds facing the data center boom. Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Brody Ford reacts to the earnings report. Plus, Anthropic’s initial public offering has drawn multiple times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz previews next weeks expected mega-IPO. Then, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Rachel Metz talks OpenAI’s quarterly revenue, which hit $10 billion for the first time, driven by strong demand for its latest artificial intelligence software. We also hear from Bloomberg Senior Editor for Tech & Strategic Industries Michael Shepard on federal investigations into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy. Finally, Bloomberg News Sustainability Editor Eric Roston breaks down how climate models missed on key predictions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Moved to Military Housing Following Iranian Threats
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is spearheading efforts to economically isolate Iran, was moved into temporary military housing after threats from the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Nikki Haley Says She's Not Running for President in 2028
item.description: Former South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley says she will not run for president in 2028 because she needs to see unity in the Republican party and members need to show they are willing to fight. Haley ran for the White House in 2024 and failed to secure the Republican nomination. She speaks on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Asks UN to Condemn $20 Million US Bounty for Nuclear Info
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi asked the United Nations and its nuclear watchdog to denounce a US reward of as much as $20 million for information on Tehran’s nuclear program.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Political Shifts Open Window for Russia Talks
item.description: Political changes in the US and elsewhere are creating a “window of opportunity” to discuss peace with Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said ahead of talks with US envoys in Dublin.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Duggan

item.title: Huang’s Trump Ties Face Scrutiny
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from DC. On today’s show, former US Ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley, Rep. Chris Deluzio (D-PA), Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis and Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nikki Haley Rules Out 2028 Run After GOP Midterm Repudiation
item.description: Former South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley ruled out a 2028 presidential run, even as she criticized the Trump administration for November’s midterm rout that handed Democrats decisive congressional majorities.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian, Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz

item.title: Nikki Haley on Nvidia Scandal, Iran and Midterms
item.description: Nikki Haley, former US ambassador to the UN, discusses the questions surrounding an alleged relationship between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. Speaking on "Balance of Power," Haley also comments on the war in Iran, the future of leadership in Israel and the results of the midterm US elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Completely Misguided' to Blame Israel for Midterm Losses, Says Nikki Haley
item.description: Former US Ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley said that Vice President JD Vance is 'completely misguided' to say that the United States' relationship with Israel is one of the reasons that Republicans faced bruising losses in the midterm elections. Haley, who also served as the Governor of South Carolina, said that the midterm losses were more due to Republicans losing than Democrats winning and that voters are looking for change from the Republican party. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Anthropic’s IPO Could Unleash a New Wave of Venture Capital
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO could have ripple effects well beyond the public markets. Canvas Ventures co-founder Rebecca Lynn says the listing could bring long-awaited liquidity back to venture capital, validate a new generation of AI-first startups and ultimately fuel fresh investment across Silicon Valley. She joins Riley Griffin on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DSA Saying ‘You’re Next’ to Jeffries Angers Black Democrats
item.description: Some of New York’s incoming congressional delegation aren’t sold on backing Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House.
item.dc:creator: Laura Nahmias

item.title: Congress Set to Subpoena Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Republicans Say
item.description: Two key House Republicans on Wednesday said Congress is prepared to subpoena Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang to provide answers about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Emily Birnbaum
